debate.name: Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Ltd

rounds.text: Conceded: SPARC has shown explosive trailing twelve-month sales growth of 2856% [E15] and trades at a low P/E of 3.92x [E1]. However, this growth has not translated into actual liquidity, as cash conversion is highly negative at -0.15x [E27], operating cash flow was negative Rs -239 Cr in Mar 2026 [E28], and working capital days have ballooned from -768 days to 215 days [E54]. To sustain operations, the company is increasingly reliant on leverage, with borrowings rising to Rs 559 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 269 Cr a year earlier [E33] and promoter-backed debt exceeding $45 million [E71], forcing management to seek a new funding plan to extend its cash window [E67]. This financial strain is compounded by critical operational risks, including potential regulatory hurdles for its PDP-716 product due to manufacturing compliance issues [E72] and a challenging development pathway for vodobatinib [E73]. Consequently, the stock trades at an expensive price-to-book ratio of 4.68x [E53] compared to the sector benchmark of 3x [E7], while long-term investors have suffered negative compounded share price growth of -5% over three years [E20] and -7% over five years [E19].
